messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated DNS error rate detected for geodns queries to eu-west-1 via Cloudflare resolver pool. Error type: SERVFAIL/timeout. 5m error rate spike > 7x baseline. Proactive paging to oncall.

matt (SRE): I'm on it. grabbing dig traces and health checks. any customer reports?

jamie (oncall): getting a couple of pings from support about 502s on api.redwood.ai for EU customers. marking P1 until we understand scope.

alexandra (support): Confirmed 3 customer threads in EU complaining about intermittent failures and slow responses starting ~10:03 UTC. Collecting customer IPs.

matt (SRE): running quick probes:
```
# from eu probe
dig +time=5 @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai A +short
;; connection timed out; server did not answer
```
Also running AWS Route53 health checks — some checks for eu-edge are failing intermittently.

leila (netops): I'm seeing increased SERVFAILs from Cloudflare resolver pools in eu-west-1 in our monitoring. Internal resolver latency to CF is spiking ~800ms. Route53 responses look fine when queried directly from us-east, but geo-routing in eu is often going through CF.

matt (SRE): hypothesis: Cloudflare resolver pool or upstream REP in that region is dropping TTLs/servfails causing clients to fallback incorrectly and some edge nodes to hit cold model cache -> 502s. Mitigation plan: 1) reduce public TTLs for critical records to 60s (so changes propagate faster), 2) enable Route53 failover to secondary endpoints for eu, 3) temporarily route eu traffic to alternate resolver path we control.

jamie (oncall): +1 to failover. what's the quick command to flip Route53 weighted record to backup?

matt (SRE): AWS CLI run:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://failover-change.json
```
failover-change.json contains a weighted/latency-based swap to `eu-backup.redwood.internal`. I'm going to stage and apply with 60s TTL.

infra-bot: Deploy request recorded: route53-change by matt — waiting approval from netops.

leila (netops): approved. I'll also open a Cloudflare ticket and attach our PCAPs. If we flip Route53, prepare to watch for increased load on eu-backup and autoscale.

matt (SRE): applying change now.
```
# applied change-batch
change-info: {"Id":"/change/C0A1B2C3","Status":"PENDING","SubmittedAt":"2026-03-15T10:15:40Z"}
```

alexandra (support): letting affected customers know we're investigating and performing routing mitigation. Drafting an update: "We're seeing elevated DNS errors in EU causing intermittent API failures. We're applying a temporary routing change; we'll update you in ~15 minutes."

jamie (oncall): after flip, I'm seeing tail latency drop on EU requests and error rate trending down in our anomaly dashboard. still some 5xxs but decreasing. :thumbsup:

leila (netops): Cloudflare support responded — they're investigating a regional resolver flapping incident affecting eu-west-1 and eu-west-2. They've identified an internal BGP flap affecting a subset of resolvers. They're implementing mitigations on their side. Link: https://support.cloudflare.com/ticket/abc-12345 (private).

matt (SRE): good. keeping Route53 failover active until CF confirms stable. pushing alert thresholds to be more sensitive so we auto-detect any relapse.

infra-bot: Autoscaling event: eu-backup pool scaled +3 instances due to increased traffic after failover.

alexandra (support): Customers updated with mitigation note. No active escalations; two customers asked for ETA for full fix — replied that we're monitoring and CF is rolling mitigations.

matt (SRE): next steps for oncall handoff: I'm going to create a short incident checklist in incidents-ticketing and tag postmortem owners: netops/leila for external provider comms, infra for capacity adjustments, and SRE for root cause verification.

jamie (oncall): handoff to matt for long-running RCA. I'll stay available for any customer escalations for next 30m then hand to night oncall.

leila (netops): Cloudflare says they'll rollback the affected BGP change and monitor for 30 minutes. If errors return, we'll trigger automatic re-route back to backup.

matt (SRE): logging timeline and evidence. capturing dig/curl samples and resolver traces. adding action item: add active external-resolver health-checks into our dashboard (we only had passive metrics).

incident-bot: Incident P1 created: "eu DNS resolver spike / CF regional flap" — incident id INC-20260315-42. Page: oncall, netops, support.

alexandra (support): tagging customers impacted in the incident ticket. We will coordinate a follow-up once CF closes their ticket.

jamie (oncall): closing the high-urgency paging loop. keep this thread for live notes. :white_check_mark:
